chapter.title: Lipid Structure and Function
chapter.scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT biochemistry lessons covering the declared outline sections. This release is implemented, not independently scientifically verified; it is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Amphipathic lipids contain both water-compatible and hydrophobic regions. Many phospholipids form bilayers with head groups facing water and tails packed inward.
Cis unsaturation introduces bends that hinder close packing. Shorter tails and more cis double bonds generally increase fluidity at otherwise similar conditions.
Cholesterol modulates packing and permeability. Its effect on fluidity depends on temperature and composition; it is not a universal fluidizer or rigidifier.
Sphingolipids and glycerophospholipids have different backbones. A membrane schematic shows organization, not atom-by-atom structure or a universal lipid ratio.

steps.text: Some lipids act as signals or signal precursors. Steroid hormones derive from cholesterol; many eicosanoids derive from polyunsaturated fatty-acid precursors.
Steroid receptors often act intracellularly to alter gene expression. Lipid derivation alone does not prove that every lipid signal uses an intracellular receptor.
Cleavage of a membrane phosphoinositide can generate diacylglycerol and a soluble inositol phosphate messenger. The two products occupy different cellular regions.
Signaling responses depend on receptor expression and downstream machinery. A circulating hormone can affect different tissues differently.

steps.text: Triacylglycerol contains glycerol esterified to three fatty acids. It is a neutral storage lipid, distinct from an amphipathic membrane phospholipid.
Fatty-acid carbons are relatively reduced and release substantial energy on oxidation. Lipid droplets store fuel with much less associated water than glycogen.
Hydrolysis releases fatty acids and glycerol for different metabolic routes. Storage lipid does not move through blood as a freely dissolved hydrophobic pool.
Energy density is a comparison per mass, not a claim that every tissue can use every lipid-derived fuel under every condition.
